rules.title: Tracking SDK present but NSUserTrackingUsageDescription is missing
rules.description: The app includes {{sdk_names}}, which access the IDFA or perform cross-app tracking. iOS requires the NSUserTrackingUsageDescription key and an AppTrackingTransparency prompt before any tracking occurs. Apple rejects builds that link tracking SDKs without this key.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer installs the app, sees ad or attribution traffic without an ATT prompt, and rejects under 5.1.2.
rules.fix: Add NSUserTrackingUsageDescription to Info.plist (or expo.ios.infoPlist / INFOPLIST_KEY_NSUserTrackingUsageDescription build setting) with a specific reason, and call ATTrackingManager.requestTrackingAuthorization before initializing {{sdk_names}}.

rules.title: Google Mobile Ads SDK present but GADApplicationIdentifier is missing
rules.description: The app includes Google Mobile Ads SDK (AdMob), which reads GADApplicationIdentifier from Info.plist during initialization and deliberately crashes the app at launch when the key is absent. This is one of the most common guaranteed-reproduction crashes App Review encounters.
rules.user_impact: The app crashes on first launch during App Review, which is an automatic 2.1 App Completeness rejection since the reviewer cannot proceed past the crash.
rules.fix: Add GADApplicationIdentifier to Info.plist with the AdMob app ID from the AdMob console (or the expo.ios.config.googleMobileAdsAppId / INFOPLIST_KEY_GADApplicationIdentifier build setting), formatted as ca-app-pub-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX~YYYYYYYYYY.

rules.title: Third-party login offered without Sign in with Apple
rules.description: The app offers {{sdk_names}} as a third-party or social login option but does not also offer Sign in with Apple. Guideline 4.8 requires apps that use a third-party or social login service to also offer an equivalent, privacy-preserving login option.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer signs up using the third-party login option, sees no Sign in with Apple button offered alongside it, and rejects under 4.8.
rules.fix: Add the Sign in with Apple capability (com.apple.developer.applesignin entitlement) using AuthenticationServices and ASAuthorizationAppleIDButton, and present it with equal prominence to the existing third-party login button.

rules.title: Account creation detected without a confirmed account-deletion flow
rules.description: The app supports account creation, but static analysis did not find an in-app account-deletion flow. Guideline 5.1.1(v) requires apps that support account creation to also offer account deletion from within the app, not only by contacting support. Detection here is heuristic since static analysis only sees a subset of the app's source, so severity is kept at medium rather than high.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer creates a test account, looks for a delete-account option in Settings or the account screen, does not find one, and rejects under 5.1.1(v).
rules.fix: Add a 'Delete Account' option, typically in Settings or the account screen, that permanently deletes the user's account and associated personal data with a confirmation step. If deletion is delayed rather than immediate, disclose the timeline to the user.

rules.title: SDK requires an Info.plist key that is missing
rules.description: A detected SDK requires the {{plist_key}} Info.plist key which is missing.
rules.user_impact: Apple's review process, or the SDK itself at runtime, treats the missing key as a functional or compliance failure specific to that SDK, ranging from a launch crash to a rejection for insufficient permission disclosure.
rules.fix: Add the {{plist_key}} key to Info.plist (or the equivalent expo.ios.infoPlist / INFOPLIST_KEY_{{plist_key}} build setting). {{reason}}

rules.title: SDK requires a privacy manifest but no privacy manifest was found
rules.description: The app includes {{sdk_names}}, which is on Apple's list of SDKs that must ship a privacy manifest. Since May 2024, apps that use these SDKs must include a PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy file, and third-party SDKs distributed as binary frameworks must include their own privacy manifest.
rules.user_impact: App Store Connect flags the missing manifest at upload with an ITMS warning, and the reviewer may reject the build under 5.1.1 for undisclosed data collection.
rules.fix: Add a PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy file to the app target declaring all Required Reason API usages with Apple's approved reason codes, and confirm {{sdk_names}} ships its own manifest, updating to the latest SDK version if it does not.

rules.title: Health app includes an advertising SDK
rules.description: The app declares HealthKit or another health capability alongside {{sdk_names}}, an advertising SDK. Guideline 1.4.1 holds health apps to greater scrutiny, and guideline 5.1.3 separately prohibits using health, fitness, or medical research data for advertising or marketing purposes.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer sees ad content inside a health-data flow and rejects the app for mixing advertising with sensitive health data, even if the ad SDK does not directly read HealthKit data.
rules.fix: Remove {{sdk_names}} from any screen that reads or displays health data, or remove the ads SDK entirely if the app's core purpose is health tracking. If ads are required elsewhere in the app, keep them fully separated from health data collection and confirm no health data reaches the ad SDK.

rules.title: Kids Category app includes an advertising or tracking SDK
rules.description: The app targets the Kids Category but includes {{sdk_names}}, which Apple treats as third-party analytics, advertising, or tracking capable of collecting identifiable information from children. Guideline 1.3 prohibits Kids Category apps from including such SDKs.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer detects the SDK in the binary or its network traffic and rejects the app under 1.3, regardless of whether the SDK is actually configured to collect data from this app's users.
rules.fix: Remove {{sdk_names}} from the Kids Category build, or replace it with a COPPA-compliant, non-identifying alternative, such as a first-party, aggregate-only analytics solution that avoids advertising identifiers, IP-based fingerprinting, and cross-app tracking.

rules.title: External payment SDK present alongside possible digital goods
rules.description: The app includes {{sdk_names}} or another external checkout path. Guideline 3.1.3(e) permits purchase methods other than In-App Purchase for physical goods and services consumed outside the app, but guideline 3.1.1 requires In-App Purchase for digital content, features, or services consumed within the app. Static analysis cannot tell which case this is.
rules.user_impact: If the external payment path sells digital content, the reviewer rejects under 3.1.1 for bypassing In-App Purchase; if it only sells physical goods or services, it is compliant as-is.
rules.fix: Confirm what the external payment path actually sells. If it unlocks digital content, features, or in-app functionality, replace it with StoreKit In-App Purchase. If it exclusively sells physical goods or services consumed outside the app, no change is required, but keep the purchase flow clearly separate from any digital unlocks.

rules.title: Subscription capability detected without a restore-purchases flow
rules.description: The app offers subscriptions but static analysis did not find a restore-purchases mechanism. Guideline 3.1.2 requires apps with auto-renewable subscriptions to let users restore previously purchased subscriptions on a new device or after reinstalling.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer reinstalls the app or switches test devices, looks for a way to restore their subscription, does not find one, and rejects under 3.1.2.
rules.fix: Add a visible 'Restore Purchases' button on the paywall or in account settings that calls Transaction.currentEntitlements (StoreKit 2) or SKPaymentQueue.restoreCompletedTransactions() (StoreKit 1), and re-enable premium features once restored transactions are verified.

rules.title: App is mostly a WebView wrapper around a website
rules.description: Most of the app's screens render through a WebView, and the app is flagged as webview-heavy. Guideline 4.2 requires apps to include native features, content, and UI that go beyond a repackaged website.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer navigates the app, sees the same experience as the mobile website in Safari, and rejects under 4.2 as a minimum-functionality violation.
rules.fix: Add native functionality that a website cannot provide, such as push notifications, offline support, native navigation, or device-specific features (Face ID, widgets, Shortcuts), or convert key flows like onboarding, checkout, and account to native UI so the WebView becomes a minority of the experience.

rules.title: Export compliance encryption key is not declared in Info.plist
rules.description: Info.plist does not declare ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption. Without this key, App Store Connect asks the export compliance question on every submission, which slows down releases and can be answered incorrectly under time pressure.
rules.user_impact: Every build upload stalls on an extra export-compliance prompt in App Store Connect, and an incorrect answer can delay release or trigger additional legal document requirements.
rules.fix: Add ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption to Info.plist: false if the app only uses standard iOS encryption such as HTTPS/TLS, or true plus the relevant export compliance documentation if the app uses proprietary or non-exempt encryption.

rules.title: Background location mode declared without a matching capability
rules.description: Info.plist declares "location" in UIBackgroundModes, but static analysis found no feature that plausibly needs location updates while the app is backgrounded. Guideline 2.5.4 only permits background modes for their intended purpose, and unused or unjustified background modes are a common rejection and Resolution Center follow-up question.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer asks why the app needs background location, and without a justified in-app feature such as live location sharing or geofenced reminders, the app is rejected or held for clarification under 2.5.4.
rules.fix: If the app has no feature that genuinely needs location while backgrounded, remove "location" from UIBackgroundModes and switch to requestWhenInUseAuthorization(). If it does, document the feature in the Notes for Review and ensure the relevant capability is actually implemented and visible to the reviewer.

rules.title: App Transport Security is disabled for all connections
rules.description: Info.plist sets NSAllowsArbitraryLoads to true under NSAppTransportSecurity, which disables App Transport Security for every network connection instead of scoping exceptions to the specific domains that need them. App Review treats a blanket ATS exception as an unjustified software requirements gap and may ask for a specific justification or reject the submission.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer sees an app-wide ATS exception with no per-domain justification and either rejects the submission or opens a Resolution Center request asking why arbitrary insecure connections are required.
rules.fix: Remove NSAllowsArbitraryLoads and instead scope exceptions per domain under NSExceptionDomains for the specific hosts that cannot yet support TLS, or migrate those endpoints to HTTPS entirely and drop the ATS exception.

rules.title: User-generated content detected without confirmed moderation controls
rules.description: The app allows users to post content, but whether the required moderation controls exist cannot be determined by static analysis alone. Guideline 1.2 requires apps with user-generated content to include a way to filter objectionable material, a mechanism to report content and abusive users with a timely response, the ability to block abusive users, and published contact information.
rules.user_impact: If any of the required controls, filtering, reporting, blocking, or published contact information, is missing, the reviewer posts test content and rejects under 1.2 once its absence is confirmed.
rules.fix: Confirm the app has all four required controls: a report or flag action on every piece of user content, a user-blocking feature, a moderation process with a stated response time, and a visible way to contact the developer, then document them in the Notes for Review since App Review cannot always find them through UI exploration alone.

rules.title: Data-collecting SDKs present but no in-app privacy policy link was found
rules.description: The app includes {{sdk_names}}, which collect analytics, advertising, attribution, or account data, but static analysis found no privacy policy link anywhere in the scanned source. Guideline 5.1.1 requires every app to include a link to its privacy policy inside the app as well as in the App Store Connect metadata field. Detection is heuristic since the link may live in server-driven content, so severity stays at medium.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer looks for the privacy policy link inside the app, typically in Settings, onboarding, or the account screen, cannot find one, and rejects under 5.1.1 even if the App Store Connect metadata field is filled in.
rules.fix: Add a visible Privacy Policy link inside the app, typically in Settings or the sign-up screen, pointing to a live page that explains what data the app and its third-party SDKs collect, how it is used, and the retention and deletion policy. Keep the same URL in the App Store Connect privacy policy field.

rules.title: NSUserTrackingUsageDescription declared but the privacy manifest says the app does not track
rules.description: Info.plist declares NSUserTrackingUsageDescription, signaling that the app intends to request App Tracking Transparency permission, but the app's PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy sets NSPrivacyTracking to false. App Store Connect cross-checks these declarations, and a tracking prompt combined with a manifest that denies tracking is an inconsistency that triggers follow-up questions or a rejection under 5.1.2.
rules.user_impact: App Store Connect or the reviewer flags the mismatch between the ATT prompt and the privacy manifest, and the submission is held until the declarations agree with each other and with the app's actual data flows.
rules.fix: Make the declarations consistent. If the app tracks users or shares data with data brokers, set NSPrivacyTracking to true and list the tracking domains in NSPrivacyTrackingDomains. If it genuinely does not track, remove NSUserTrackingUsageDescription and the ATT prompt instead.

rules.title: Ads SDK present but Info.plist declares no SKAdNetworkItems
rules.description: The app includes {{sdk_names}} but Info.plist contains no SKAdNetworkItems entries. SKAdNetwork is Apple's privacy-preserving attribution framework, and ad networks rely on their SKAdNetwork identifiers being listed in the app's Info.plist to attribute installs when App Tracking Transparency consent is denied. This does not cause a rejection, but it silently degrades campaign attribution and ad revenue reporting.
rules.user_impact: No rejection risk. Install attribution for ad campaigns degrades because SKAdNetwork postbacks cannot be matched to the ad networks serving this app's ads, which hurts monetization reporting rather than the review outcome.
rules.fix: Add the SKAdNetworkItems array to Info.plist with the SKAdNetworkIdentifier values each integrated ad network publishes in its integration docs, and keep the list in sync when adding mediation partners.

rules.title: Real-money gaming features require licensing and geo-restrictions
rules.description: The app appears to offer gambling, betting, or lottery functionality. Guideline 5.3.4 requires apps offering real money gaming or lotteries to have the necessary licensing and permissions in every location where the app is available, to be geo-restricted to those locations, and to be free on the App Store. Static analysis cannot confirm licensing, so this always needs manual verification.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer asks for proof of gambling licenses for every storefront where the app is distributed, and rejects or removes the app if licensing, geo-restriction, or the developer's organization enrollment cannot be demonstrated.
rules.fix: Restrict the app's App Store availability to territories where you hold valid gambling licenses, attach the licensing documentation in the Notes for Review, keep the app free to download, and make sure the developer account is enrolled as an organization rather than an individual.

rules.title: Cryptocurrency features are restricted to enrolled organizations and approved use cases
rules.description: The app appears to include cryptocurrency functionality such as a wallet, exchange, or token features. Guideline 3.1.5(b) only allows crypto wallets from developers enrolled as organizations, forbids on-device mining, restricts exchange features to the exchanges themselves, and requires ICO functionality to come from established financial institutions. Static analysis cannot determine which case applies, so this always needs manual verification.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer checks the developer's enrollment type and the app's crypto features against 3.1.5(b), and rejects if a wallet ships from an individual account, if any mining runs on the device, or if exchange functionality is offered by a party other than the exchange itself.
rules.fix: Confirm the developer account is enrolled as an organization, remove any on-device mining, and if the app offers exchange or ICO functionality, confirm it is offered directly by the licensed exchange or institution. Document regulatory approvals in the Notes for Review.

rules.title: AI-generated content needs moderation and reporting controls
rules.description: The app appears to generate content with AI. App Review applies guideline 1.2's user-generated content standards to AI-generated content: the app needs filtering of objectionable material, a way for users to report problematic output, and an age rating that matches what the generator can produce. Apps that can generate adult or abusive content without guardrails are rejected. Whether these controls exist is behavioral, so this always needs manual verification.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer prompts the AI feature with borderline requests, and rejects under 1.2 or demands a 17+ age rating if the app produces objectionable content without filtering, reporting, or blocking controls.
rules.fix: Add server-side content filtering for AI output, an in-app report action on generated content, and a block mechanism where user-to-user sharing exists, then set the age rating to match what the generator can actually produce and describe the moderation pipeline in the Notes for Review.

rules.title: Audio background mode declared but background playback cannot be confirmed
rules.description: Info.plist declares "audio" in UIBackgroundModes, which is only permitted for apps that actually play audible content while backgrounded, such as music, podcast, or navigation apps. Whether this app truly plays background audio is behavioral, so it needs verification. Declaring the mode without real background playback is a common 2.5.4 rejection.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer backgrounds the app, hears no ongoing audio and finds no feature that needs it, and rejects under 2.5.4 for declaring a background mode the app does not use for its intended purpose.
rules.fix: If the app plays ongoing audio in the background, keep the mode and point the reviewer to the feature in the Notes for Review. If not, remove "audio" from UIBackgroundModes; apps that only play short foreground sounds do not need it.

rules.title: remote-notification background mode declared without any push notification setup
rules.description: Info.plist declares "remote-notification" in UIBackgroundModes, but no push notification SDK was detected and the entitlements do not declare aps-environment. Background remote notifications only work for apps that actually receive push notifications, and an unused background mode is flagged under 2.5.4.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer or an automated check questions why the app wakes for remote notifications it can never receive, which triggers a Resolution Center question or a 2.5.4 rejection for declaring an unneeded background mode.
rules.fix: Remove "remote-notification" from UIBackgroundModes if the app does not receive push notifications. If it should, add the Push Notifications capability so the aps-environment entitlement is generated, and register for remote notifications in code.

rules.title: Kids Category app collects health data
rules.description: The app targets the Kids Category while also using HealthKit or another health data source. Guideline 5.1.4 subjects apps for kids to strict data collection limits and children's privacy law compliance such as COPPA and GDPR-K, and guideline 1.3 prohibits sending personally identifiable or device data from kids apps to third parties. Health data collection in a kids app draws the strictest review and is rejected without documented parental consent flows and a clear justification.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer sees health or sensor data collection in an app aimed at children and rejects under 5.1.4 unless the app demonstrates verifiable parental consent and a core feature that genuinely requires that data.
rules.fix: Remove health data collection from the Kids Category build, or if it is essential to the app's core purpose, implement verifiable parental consent before any collection, minimize what is collected, keep it off third-party services, and explain the flow in the Notes for Review.

rules.title: Contacts access alongside advertising SDKs risks undisclosed data sharing
rules.description: The app reads the user's contacts and also includes {{sdk_names}}. Guideline 5.1.2 forbids using, transmitting, or sharing personal data such as the address book without explicit permission for that purpose, and sharing contact data with advertising SDKs is treated as repurposing data that was collected for a different feature. Whether contact data actually reaches the ad SDK is behavioral, so this needs verification.
rules.user_impact: If review determines contact data is available to the advertising stack without separate consent, the app is rejected under 5.1.2, and a live app can face expedited removal for the same finding.
rules.fix: Keep contacts data strictly inside the feature that needs it, confirm the ad SDKs are configured without access to contact fields, and disclose contacts collection in the privacy nutrition label. If contacts are only used for an invite feature, say so in the Notes for Review.

rules.title: VoIP background mode declared but calling functionality cannot be confirmed
rules.description: Info.plist declares "voip" in UIBackgroundModes. Since iOS 13, VoIP push notifications must be reported to CallKit as incoming calls, and the voip background mode is only permitted for apps with real voice calling functionality. Apps that declare it for keep-alive pings or silent wake-ups are rejected under 2.5.4. Whether this app implements real calling is behavioral, so it needs verification.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer looks for an actual calling feature, and rejects under 2.5.4 if the voip mode exists only to keep the app alive in the background or to deliver silent wake-ups.
rules.fix: If the app offers voice calls, integrate CallKit and report every VoIP push as an incoming call. If it does not, remove "voip" from UIBackgroundModes and deliver messages through regular push notifications.

rules.title: Always location permission requested where When In Use may be sufficient
rules.description: Info.plist declares an Always location usage description, which requests location access even while the app is not in use. App Review regularly challenges Always access and asks developers to justify why When In Use authorization is not sufficient, since iOS 13 made When In Use plus background updates cover most legitimate use cases. Whether this app's features genuinely need Always access is behavioral, so it needs verification.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer or a Resolution Center follow-up asks what feature needs location while the app is closed, and the submission is held or rejected until the justification is convincing or the request is downgraded to When In Use.
rules.fix: Audit the features that consume location. If geofencing, background tracking, or automatic check-ins genuinely run without the app open, keep Always access and explain the feature in the Notes for Review. Otherwise request only When In Use authorization and remove the Always usage descriptions.

rules.title: Health data collected without a confirmed privacy policy link
rules.description: The app collects health data, but static analysis found no privacy policy link in the scanned source. Apps that access HealthKit or other health data must provide a privacy policy explaining exactly how health data is used and stored, and guidelines 5.1.1 and 5.1.3 hold health data to stricter standards than ordinary usage data. Detection is heuristic since the link may live in server-driven content, so severity stays at medium.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer checks the app and its metadata for a privacy policy that covers health data handling, and rejects under 5.1.1 when it is missing, incomplete, or silent about HealthKit.
rules.fix: Publish a privacy policy that explicitly covers what health data the app reads and writes, how it is stored, that it is never shared for advertising, and how users can delete it, then link it inside the app and in App Store Connect.

rules.title: Privacy manifest declares tracking but NSUserTrackingUsageDescription is missing
rules.description: The app's PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy sets NSPrivacyTracking to true, declaring that the app or its SDKs track users across apps and websites, but Info.plist does not declare NSUserTrackingUsageDescription. A tracking declaration without the ATT usage description means the app can never present the required App Tracking Transparency prompt, which violates 5.1.2.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer sees a manifest that declares tracking, verifies that no ATT prompt can ever appear because the usage description is missing, and rejects under 5.1.2 for tracking without obtaining permission.
rules.fix: Add NSUserTrackingUsageDescription to Info.plist with a specific reason and request ATTrackingManager authorization before any tracking or IDFA access occurs, or if the app genuinely stopped tracking, set NSPrivacyTracking to false and clear NSPrivacyTrackingDomains.

rules.title: Health features may require medical disclaimers and methodology disclosure
rules.description: The app works with health data, and guideline 1.4.1 reviews medical and health apps with greater scrutiny. Apps that could provide inaccurate readings, make diagnostic claims, or present health measurements must disclose the data and methodology behind those claims, and drug dosage calculators are restricted to approved entities under 1.4.2. What the app actually claims is behavioral, so this always needs manual verification.
rules.user_impact: The reviewer examines health-related claims in the app and its metadata, and rejects under 1.4.1 when measurement or diagnostic features lack supporting methodology, disclaimers, or regulatory clearance where required.
rules.fix: Add clear disclaimers that the app does not provide medical advice, cite the methodology or studies behind any measurement features, avoid diagnostic language unless you hold regulatory clearance, and describe data sources in the Notes for Review.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app uses a third-party payment system (Stripe) for digital content that must use In-App Purchase.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Integrated Stripe checkout to sell premium digital features like custom themes, advanced filters, and exclusive content within the app. Digital goods and services consumed within the app must use Apple's In-App Purchase system.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.1 - Business - Payments - In-App Purchase: Your app uses a third-party payment mechanism (Stripe) for digital content, features, or services that are consumed within the app. Per App Store Review Guidelines, apps offering digital goods or services for consumption within the app must use In-App Purchase. Please implement StoreKit for all digital content purchases.
stories.fix: Replaced Stripe checkout with Apple's StoreKit 2 for all digital goods purchases. Stripe was kept only for physical goods/services not consumed within the app (if applicable). Implemented IAP products in App Store Connect for all premium features.
behavioralSignals: credit card form for premium features

stories.rejectionReason: Your app does not include a mechanism to restore previously purchased subscriptions.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Implemented a subscription paywall but did not include a 'Restore Purchases' button. Users who reinstalled the app or switched devices had no way to restore their active subscriptions without re-purchasing.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.2 - Business - Payments - Subscriptions: Your app does not include a 'Restore Purchases' mechanism. Apps that offer auto-renewable subscriptions must include a restore mechanism to allow users to restore their previously purchased subscriptions on a new device or after reinstalling the app.
stories.fix: Added a clearly visible 'Restore Purchases' button on the subscription/paywall screen. Implemented the SKPaymentQueue.restoreCompletedTransactions() (or StoreKit 2 equivalent) to restore active subscriptions. Also added a restore option in the app settings.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app does not clearly display auto-renewable subscription terms before the purchase is initiated.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Displayed a subscription paywall with pricing and a 'Subscribe' button but did not include the required auto-renewal terms, such as the subscription duration, price per period, and that the subscription automatically renews unless cancelled at least 24 hours before the end of the current period.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.2 - Business - Payments - Subscriptions: Your app does not clearly display the following required subscription information before the user completes the purchase: the price and duration of the subscription, that payment will be charged to the iTunes Account, that the subscription automatically renews unless auto-renew is turned off at least 24 hours before the end of the current period, and links to your Privacy Policy and Terms of Use.
stories.fix: Added all required subscription terms directly on the paywall screen in legible text. Included: price per period, subscription duration, auto-renewal disclosure, cancellation instructions, and links to Privacy Policy and Terms of Use. The terms are displayed before the subscribe button so users see them before purchasing.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app contains a link that directs users to an external payment mechanism for digital content.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Included a button or link in the app labeled 'Upgrade to Premium' that opened the developer's website pricing page where users could purchase premium digital features via Stripe or PayPal, bypassing Apple's IAP system.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.1 - Business - Payments - In-App Purchase: Your app includes a link that directs users to an external mechanism for purchases that should be made through In-App Purchase. Specifically, tapping 'Upgrade to Premium' opens a web page where users can purchase premium features. Apps may not include buttons, external links, or other calls to action that direct users to purchasing mechanisms other than IAP for digital content.
stories.fix: Removed the external payment link entirely. Replaced the web-based upgrade flow with StoreKit In-App Purchase. If eligible for the External Link Account Entitlement (reader apps, music streaming, etc.), applied for the entitlement with proper commission arrangements.

stories.rejectionReason: Your In-App Purchase products failed to load during review.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: IAP products worked correctly in the sandbox testing environment but failed to load during App Review. The products were not in the correct status in App Store Connect (they were still 'Waiting for Review' or 'Missing Metadata'), causing StoreKit to return empty product arrays.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.1 - Business - Payments - In-App Purchase: We were unable to purchase the In-App Purchase products in your app. When we attempted to view your subscription options, no products were displayed. Please ensure your IAP products are properly configured and in the correct status.
stories.fix: Ensured all IAP products were in 'Ready to Submit' status in App Store Connect before submitting the app binary. Verified product IDs matched exactly between the app code and App Store Connect. Submitted the IAP products for review alongside the app binary. Added error handling UI to show a message and retry button when products fail to load.

stories.rejectionReason: The subscription price displayed in your app does not match the price configured in App Store Connect.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Hardcoded the subscription price as '$4.99/month' in the app UI, but the actual price in App Store Connect was set to $9.99/month. The mismatch was caught during review when the reviewer compared the displayed price with the StoreKit payment sheet price.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.2 - Business - Payments - Subscriptions: The subscription price displayed in your app ($4.99/month) does not match the price set in App Store Connect ($9.99/month). The pricing information displayed to users must accurately reflect the actual purchase price.
stories.fix: Removed all hardcoded prices from the app UI. Instead, used StoreKit's Product.displayPrice property to dynamically fetch and display the current price from App Store Connect. This also ensures correct pricing is shown across different currencies and regions.
behavioralSignals: different price in UI vs payment sheet
price doesn't match App Store Connect

stories.rejectionReason: Your app offers no functionality without a paid subscription and the free trial provides no usable experience.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Created an app where all content was behind a paywall. The app offered a '7-day free trial' but immediately required payment information and locked users into a subscription. There was no lite/free tier to explore the app's functionality before committing to a purchase.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.2 - Business - Payments - Subscriptions: Your app locks users into a subscription immediately with no way to experience the app's core functionality before purchasing. Apps should provide some level of access or a meaningful free experience so users can evaluate the app before subscribing.
stories.fix: Added a limited free tier that allows users to access basic features without subscribing. Users can create up to 3 items, view content with ads, and explore the app's core functionality. The premium subscription removes limits and ads. Also ensured the free trial doesn't require payment information upfront.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app offers randomized virtual items for purchase (loot boxes) without disclosing the probability of receiving each type of item.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Built a mobile game with gacha/loot box mechanics where players could purchase virtual item packs with random contents using IAP, but did not disclose the drop rates or probability of receiving each rarity tier of items.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.1 - Business - Payments - In-App Purchase: Your app offers loot boxes or other mechanisms that provide randomized virtual items for purchase but does not disclose the odds of receiving each type of item to the user prior to purchase. Apps offering such mechanisms must include the probability of each type of item before the user commits to the purchase.
stories.fix: Added a 'Drop Rates' information button next to every loot box purchase option. The button displays a clear breakdown of probabilities for each item rarity tier (e.g., Common: 60%, Rare: 25%, Epic: 10%, Legendary: 5%). This information is shown before the purchase confirmation.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app uses Stripe for a tipping/donation feature for digital content creators, which must use In-App Purchase.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Askaloo (a Q&A platform) implemented a tipping feature using Stripe where users could tip content creators directly via credit card payments within the app, bypassing Apple's IAP system for what Apple classified as digital content consumption.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.1 - Business - Payments - In-App Purchase: Your app uses a third-party payment mechanism (Stripe) for tips/donations to content creators. Tips for digital content or services consumed within the app are considered digital goods and must use In-App Purchase. Please implement IAP for all tipping functionality.
stories.fix: Replaced Stripe tipping with Apple's In-App Purchase consumable items for tip amounts. Created IAP products for different tip tiers ($1, $5, $10, $25). While Apple takes its commission on IAP transactions, this was the only way to keep the tipping feature in the app.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app appears to be a white-label or template app that is not sufficiently differentiated.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Submitted a payment processing app that was a white-labeled version of a payment platform SDK. Multiple nearly identical apps from different business accounts used the same codebase with only branding differences (logo, colors, business name).
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.2.2 - Business - Other Business Model Issues - Unacceptable: Your app is a white-label version of another app. We have identified multiple apps with the same binary that differ only in branding. Creating multiple apps from a template or app generation service is considered spam and is not permitted on the App Store.
stories.fix: Instead of publishing separate white-label apps for each business, consolidated into a single app with multi-tenant support. Each business gets their own branded experience within the single app through configuration. Alternatively, if each business has significantly unique features, ensured each version has meaningful functional differences beyond just branding.
behavioralSignals: multiple similar apps from same codebase

stories.rejectionReason: Hardcoded pricing in your app does not match the prices configured in App Store Connect.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Displayed hardcoded pricing strings throughout the app (e.g., 'Premium: $2.99/mo') that were set during development. When the pricing was later changed in App Store Connect to $4.99/mo, the hardcoded strings were not updated, creating a price mismatch.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.2 - Business - Payments - Subscriptions: We noticed that the pricing displayed in your app does not match the actual subscription pricing in App Store Connect. Your app shows '$2.99/month' but the configured price is '$4.99/month'. Please ensure pricing accuracy.
stories.fix: Replaced all hardcoded price strings with dynamic pricing fetched from StoreKit. Used Product.displayPrice to show localized, accurate pricing that automatically reflects the current App Store Connect configuration and the user's local currency.

stories.rejectionReason: Your subscription products are still in review and cannot be tested.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Submitted an app update that referenced new IAP subscription products, but the products were submitted separately and were still pending review. The app binary was approved but the subscriptions remained in 'Waiting for Review' status for weeks, preventing the update from being published.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Your app has been approved, but the In-App Purchase products associated with this version are still in review. Your app update cannot be released until all associated IAP products are also approved. Please wait for the IAP review to complete.
stories.fix: For future submissions, ensured IAP products were submitted and approved before or simultaneously with the app binary. Contacted App Review via the Resolution Center to expedite the IAP review. Used the 'Submit with next app update' option in App Store Connect to link IAP products to the app submission.

stories.rejectionReason: Your In-App Purchase product metadata language does not match the primary language of your app.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Configured IAP product names and descriptions in English in App Store Connect, but the app's primary language and storefront was set to Japanese. The IAP purchase sheet displayed English text in a Japanese-language app, creating an inconsistent user experience.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.1 - Business - Payments - In-App Purchase: Your In-App Purchase product names and descriptions are in English, but your app's primary language is Japanese. Please localize your IAP product metadata to match the primary language of your app for each storefront where it is available.
stories.fix: Added Japanese localizations for all IAP product names and descriptions in App Store Connect. Used the App Store Connect localization features to provide product metadata in all languages the app supports.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app includes a link to an external purchase mechanism in an error message.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: When a user hit a feature limit, the app displayed an error message saying 'You've reached the free limit. Upgrade at https://example.com/pricing to unlock unlimited access.' This URL led to a web checkout page with Stripe payment, bypassing IAP.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.1 - Business - Payments - In-App Purchase: Your app directs users to an external purchase mechanism in an error message. Specifically, when reaching a feature limit, the app displays a URL to your website's pricing page. Apps may not direct users to external purchase mechanisms for digital content, even in error messages or alerts.
stories.fix: Removed the external URL from the error message. Replaced it with a button that opens the in-app subscription/purchase screen powered by StoreKit IAP. The error message now reads 'You've reached the free limit. Tap Upgrade to unlock unlimited access.' with an IAP-powered upgrade flow.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app uses PayPal to sell premium digital features that must use In-App Purchase.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Integrated PayPal checkout to sell premium digital features like ad removal, additional storage, and advanced editing tools within a photo editing app.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.1 - Business - Payments - In-App Purchase: Your app uses PayPal as a payment mechanism for digital content and features consumed within the app. Specifically, the 'Remove Ads' and 'Pro Editing Tools' purchases use PayPal checkout. Digital goods must be purchased through In-App Purchase.
stories.fix: Removed PayPal integration for all digital goods. Implemented StoreKit In-App Purchase for the 'Remove Ads' (non-consumable) and 'Pro Tools' (subscription) products. PayPal can only be kept for physical goods or services delivered outside the app.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app's business model has changed significantly, triggering a full re-review.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: An app that was previously approved as a free utility added a subscription paywall in an update that locked core features behind payment. Apple flagged this as a significant business model change and conducted a thorough re-review, questioning whether the app provided enough value to justify the subscription.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.2 - Business - Other Business Model Issues: Your app has undergone a significant business model change from a free utility to a paid subscription service. We need to re-evaluate whether the app's functionality justifies the subscription pricing and whether existing users are adequately served by the new model.
stories.fix: Grandfathered existing users into the premium features they previously had for free. Added a meaningful free tier with core functionality intact. Ensured the subscription provided clear additional value beyond what was previously free. Provided detailed notes in the resolution center explaining the business model change.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app charges users for iCloud storage sync which is a system-level capability.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Created a notes app that locked iCloud sync behind a paid subscription. While the app stored data locally for free, accessing your own data across devices via iCloud required purchasing the premium subscription.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.3 - Business - Payments: Your app charges users for iCloud sync functionality, which leverages system-level capabilities. You should not create a purchase to gate access to Apple system features that users expect as standard functionality.
stories.fix: Made basic iCloud sync available to all users for free. Restructured the subscription to provide value through advanced features (collaboration, advanced organization, export options) rather than gating system-level sync functionality.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app charges for access to built-in iOS capabilities.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Built an app that charged a subscription fee to enable features that are essentially wrappers around built-in iOS capabilities like the flashlight, compass, and level tool, without adding meaningful additional value.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.2.2 - Business - Other Business Model Issues: Your app charges users for functionality that duplicates built-in iOS capabilities (flashlight, compass, level) without providing sufficient additional value or unique features. Apps should not monetize basic system functionality.
stories.fix: Added significant unique value beyond the system capabilities: custom lighting modes, measurement history with export, AR-based measurements, and professional calibration tools. The subscription was repositioned around these genuinely unique features rather than the basic system functionality wrappers.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app does not include instructions for how to manage or cancel a subscription.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Implemented subscription IAP but did not include any information in the app about how users can manage their subscription, view renewal dates, or cancel through iOS Settings.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.2 - Business - Payments - Subscriptions: Your app does not include information about how to manage subscriptions. You must provide a link or instructions within the app that direct users to their subscription management settings where they can manage or cancel their subscription.
stories.fix: Added a 'Manage Subscription' button in the app settings that deep-links to the iOS subscription management page (using UIApplication.open(URL(string: 'https://apps.apple.com/account/subscriptions')!)). Also added text explaining how to cancel and when the next renewal date is.
behavioralSignals: no way to manage subscription in app

stories.rejectionReason: Your app requires a subscription with no way to use the app without payment.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Launched an app with a hard paywall that showed the subscription screen immediately on launch with no dismiss button. Users could not access any part of the app without purchasing a subscription first, with no free trial or lite functionality.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.2 - Business - Payments - Subscriptions: Your app requires a subscription purchase to access any content or functionality, with no free tier, trial, or sample content available. Users should be able to evaluate the app and experience some functionality before being required to purchase.
stories.fix: Added a dismissible paywall with a 'Continue with Free' option. Created a free tier with limited but meaningful functionality (3 sessions per day, basic features). Added a 7-day free trial option for the full premium experience. The paywall is shown after the user has had a chance to experience the app.
behavioralSignals: paywall on launch with no dismiss

stories.rejectionReason: We were unable to review your app because no demo account credentials were provided.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Submitted an app that requires login to access core functionality but did not provide demo account credentials in the App Review Information section of App Store Connect. The reviewer could not sign in and therefore could not review the app.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 2.1 - Performance - App Completeness: We are unable to complete the review of your app because we need a demo account to fully access your app's features. Please provide demo account credentials (username and password) in the App Review Information section of App Store Connect.
stories.fix: Created a dedicated demo/review account with full access to all features. Added the username and password in App Store Connect > App Information > App Review Information > Sign-in required. Included notes describing which features to test and any special setup instructions.

stories.rejectionReason: The demo account requires SMS-based two-factor authentication that the reviewer cannot complete.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Provided demo account credentials but the account required SMS-based 2FA. The verification code was sent to the developer's phone number, and the Apple reviewer in California had no way to receive or enter the code.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 2.1 - Performance - App Completeness: We were unable to log in to your app with the provided demo credentials. The account requires SMS verification and we are unable to receive the verification code. Please provide a demo account that can be fully accessed without additional verification steps or provide a way for us to complete the verification.
stories.fix: Created a review-specific account with 2FA disabled. Alternatively, if 2FA cannot be disabled: set up a shared email account where the reviewer can receive verification codes, or use TOTP-based 2FA and share the TOTP secret/QR code in the review notes so the reviewer can generate codes themselves.

stories.rejectionReason: Your support URL does not provide a way for users to contact you.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Provided a support URL in App Store Connect that linked to a generic company homepage, a blank page, or a page without any contact form, email address, phone number, or other way for users to get support.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 2.3 - Performance - Accurate Metadata: The support URL you provided does not include any contact information or mechanism for users to reach you for support. The support URL must provide a way for users to contact you with questions or issues about your app.
stories.fix: Created a dedicated support page with a contact form, support email address, and FAQ section. The page is accessible without login and provides clear ways for users to report issues and get help. Updated the support URL in App Store Connect.
behavioralSignals: no contact form on support page

stories.rejectionReason: We need a video demonstration to understand how your app works.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Submitted an app with hardware-dependent features (Bluetooth device pairing, AR experiences, IoT integration, or features requiring specific real-world conditions) that the Apple reviewer could not test in their office environment.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 2.1 - Performance - App Completeness: We are unable to fully evaluate your app's functionality because it requires specific hardware or real-world conditions we cannot replicate. Please provide a video that demonstrates the app's complete functionality, including the features that require external hardware or specific conditions.
stories.fix: Recorded a clear screen recording (or combination of screen + physical demo) showing the app's full functionality. Uploaded the video to an accessible URL (YouTube unlisted, Dropbox, etc.) and included the link in the App Review notes. The video showed: device pairing, feature usage, and all key user flows.

stories.rejectionReason: Your macOS app's Full Disk Access permission is not displaying correctly in System Preferences.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Built a macOS app that required Full Disk Access for backup or file management functionality. Due to a macOS bug, the app's entry in System Preferences > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access was not showing the correct app name or icon, making it impossible for the reviewer to grant the permission.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 2.1 - Performance - App Completeness: We were unable to grant Full Disk Access to your app. The app does not appear correctly in the Full Disk Access section of System Preferences. Without this permission, we cannot test the app's core functionality.
stories.fix: Ensured the app is properly code-signed and notarized. Added the correct bundle identifier and app name in Info.plist. For the macOS bug: provided detailed instructions in the review notes on how to manually add the app to Full Disk Access via the '+' button. Filed a Feedback with Apple about the System Preferences display issue.
behavioralSignals: app not showing in Full Disk Access

stories.rejectionReason: Your previously approved app has been removed from the App Store and re-rejected upon resubmission.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Doppel AI was initially approved and published on the App Store. It was later removed by Apple for guideline concerns (potentially related to deepfake/AI-generated content of real people). When the developer attempted to resubmit with modifications, the app was rejected again with additional scrutiny.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Your app was previously removed from the App Store for guideline violations. Upon re-review, we have determined that the app still does not comply with the App Store Review Guidelines. Your app creates AI-generated likenesses of real people, which raises concerns under Guidelines 1.1 and 5.1 regarding user safety and privacy.
stories.fix: The developer had to fundamentally rethink the app's approach to AI-generated content. Added consent verification for any real person whose likeness is generated, removed the ability to create content of public figures without authorization, implemented content safety filters, and added clear labeling of all AI-generated content.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app's deep link handling is broken, causing incorrect navigation.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: The app's Universal Links and deep link handling broke after an iOS 18 update. Deep links from emails and web pages either opened Safari instead of the app, opened the app to the wrong screen, or caused a redirect loop between the app and Safari.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 2.1 - Performance - App Completeness: We found that deep links to your app do not work correctly. Tapping a link that should open your app instead opens Safari, or opens the app to an incorrect screen. Please ensure your app's deep link handling works correctly on iOS 18.
stories.fix: Updated the Apple App Site Association (AASA) file to use the new format compatible with iOS 18. Verified the AASA file is served with the correct Content-Type (application/json). Updated the app's URL handling code to use the new UIScene-based URL handling. Tested all deep link scenarios on iOS 18 devices.
behavioralSignals: deep links open Safari instead of app
redirect loop between app and Safari

stories.rejectionReason: Your cryptocurrency wallet app does not comply with regulatory requirements for the regions where it operates.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Submitted a cryptocurrency wallet app that allowed users to buy, sell, and trade cryptocurrencies but did not have the required financial services licenses or registrations for the jurisdictions where it planned to operate.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 3.1.5(b) - Business - Cryptocurrencies: Your app facilitates cryptocurrency transactions but does not appear to comply with applicable legal requirements. Cryptocurrency exchanges and wallets must be offered by enrolled developers that are licensed or registered to provide such services in the jurisdictions where the app is available.
stories.fix: Restricted the app's availability to jurisdictions where the company holds valid licenses. Provided Apple with documentation of regulatory compliance (money transmitter licenses, FinCEN registration, etc.). Added required legal disclosures, terms of service, and risk warnings within the app.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app bundle exceeds the maximum allowed size.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Submitted an app whose total bundle size (including all architectures and resources) exceeded 4GB. The app included large uncompressed assets, multiple video files, and unoptimized images that pushed the binary size over Apple's limit.
stories.whatAppleSaid: ERROR ITMS-90381: The app's total uncompressed size exceeds the maximum allowed size of 4GB. Your app bundle (including all architectures) is approximately 4.7GB. Please reduce the size of your app.
stories.fix: Used On-Demand Resources (ODR) to host large assets on Apple's servers and download them only when needed. Compressed image and video assets. Used Asset Catalogs with app slicing to deliver only the assets needed for each device. Moved large content to a post-install download with user consent.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app requires users to accept push notifications to use the app.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Displayed the push notification permission dialog on launch and, if the user denied it, showed a blocking screen that prevented access to the app until notifications were enabled. The app essentially held core functionality hostage to push notification consent.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 5.1.1 - Legal - Privacy: Your app requires users to grant push notification permission to access the app's functionality. Users must be able to use your app's core features without being required to accept push notifications. Permission requests must be optional and the app must remain functional if the user declines.
stories.fix: Made push notification permission optional. Removed the blocking screen. The app now functions fully without push notifications enabled. Added a gentle, non-blocking prompt explaining the benefits of notifications at a contextually appropriate moment (e.g., after booking an appointment: 'Would you like to receive reminders?').
behavioralSignals: can't use app without push enabled

stories.rejectionReason: Your app requests 'Always' location permission when 'While Using' would be sufficient.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Requested 'Always' location permission (requestAlwaysAuthorization) for a restaurant finder app that only needed location while the user was actively browsing. Background location was not needed for any user-facing feature.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 5.1.2 - Legal - Privacy - Data Use and Sharing: Your app requests Always location authorization, but your app's use of location appears to only require 'While Using the App' authorization. Please request the minimum level of location access necessary for your app's functionality.
stories.fix: Changed from requestAlwaysAuthorization() to requestWhenInUseAuthorization(). Updated NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription with a clear description. Removed NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription and NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription from Info.plist since background location is not needed.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app's location permission flow does not account for the iOS 13+ provisional 'Allow Once' behavior.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: The app requested Always location permission, but starting with iOS 13, the system no longer shows 'Always Allow' as an option in the initial prompt. Instead, iOS shows 'Allow While Using App', 'Allow Once', and 'Don't Allow'. The 'Always' option only appears later as a separate system prompt if the app demonstrates legitimate background location usage.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 5.1.2 - Legal - Privacy - Data Use and Sharing: Your app's location permission handling does not properly adapt to iOS 13+ behavior. The app expects Always location authorization but the initial system prompt no longer offers this option. Please update your app to gracefully handle the provisional 'While Using' permission and request escalation to Always only when justified.
stories.fix: Updated the permission flow to first request When In Use authorization, then request Always authorization as a separate step. Handled the CLAuthorizationStatus.authorizedWhenInUse state gracefully. The app now works with When In Use and only prompts for escalation to Always when the user triggers a feature that genuinely requires background location.
behavioralSignals: doesn't handle When In Use fallback

stories.rejectionReason: Your app's metadata language does not match the primary language of the app.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Submitted an app where the App Store metadata (title, subtitle, description, keywords) was in English, but the app's UI was entirely in Korean. Or vice versa: app was in English but metadata was submitted in another language's storefront.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 2.3 - Performance - Accurate Metadata: Your app's App Store metadata language does not match the primary language of your app. The app description and title are in English, but the app's interface is in Korean. Please ensure your metadata language matches your app's primary language for each localization.
stories.fix: Matched the App Store metadata language to the app's primary language for each localization. Added proper localized metadata for each language the app supports. Used App Store Connect's localization feature to provide language-specific metadata for each storefront.
behavioralSignals: metadata in different language than app

stories.rejectionReason: Your app's release notes contain irrelevant or inappropriate content.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Used the release notes field for promotional messaging ('SALE: 50% off premium!'), internal development notes ('Fixed Bob's bug from Sprint 23'), social media links, or unrelated commentary instead of describing what changed in the update.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 2.3 - Performance - Accurate Metadata: Your app's release notes contain content that is not relevant to the app update. Release notes should describe what is new or changed in the current version. Please update your release notes to accurately describe the changes in this update.
stories.fix: Rewrote release notes to focus on user-facing changes: new features, bug fixes, and improvements. Removed promotional content, internal references, and unrelated commentary. Example: 'What's New: - Fixed an issue where photos wouldn't save correctly. - Improved loading speed for the feed. - Added dark mode support.'

stories.rejectionReason: Your app's metadata contains emoji characters which are not permitted in certain fields.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Used emoji characters in the app name, subtitle, or description in App Store Connect. While some apps have emojis in their metadata, Apple's enforcement is inconsistent - some apps get rejected while similar apps with emojis remain published.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 2.3 - Performance - Accurate Metadata: Your app's name/subtitle includes emoji characters. App names and subtitles should use only standard text characters. Please remove emoji from your app name and subtitle. Note: emoji may be acceptable in the app description in some cases.
stories.fix: Removed all emoji characters from the app name and subtitle fields. Emojis can sometimes be used in the longer description field, but it's safest to avoid them entirely. Used descriptive text instead of emoji to convey the app's purpose.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app is primarily a repackaged website using a web view, without sufficient native iOS functionality.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Submitted an app that was essentially a WKWebView loading the company's responsive website. The app had no native UI elements, no offline functionality, no push notifications, and no device-specific features. It was indistinguishable from visiting the website in Safari.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.2 - Design - Minimum Functionality: Your app is essentially a repackaged version of your website. We encourage you to review your app concept and incorporate native iOS features and functionality. Apps that are simply web views of a website are not appropriate for the App Store. Consider using Safari or creating a Home Screen bookmark instead.
stories.fix: Added native iOS features: push notifications for order updates, Face ID authentication, native navigation with tab bar, offline caching of key content, Haptic feedback on interactions, widgets for quick access, and Shortcuts integration. Converted critical screens (login, checkout, profile) to native SwiftUI views.
behavioralSignals: entire app is a web view

stories.rejectionReason: Your app provides only static information that would be better suited as a website.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Created a church information app that displayed static content: service times, address, staff directory, and a few pages of text about the church. No dynamic features, no community interaction, no event calendar updates, and no push notifications.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.2 - Design - Minimum Functionality: Your app provides limited functionality that could be accomplished with a website. The static information displayed (service times, address, staff bios) does not provide a compelling native app experience. We encourage you to add features that take advantage of the device's capabilities.
stories.fix: Added dynamic features: live-updating event calendar with push notification reminders, sermon audio/video streaming with offline downloads, community prayer request board (with UGC moderation), in-app giving via IAP, location-based check-in, and an interactive Bible study feature with notes.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app's user interface appears to be a web-based experience that does not follow iOS design conventions.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Built an app using Ionic/React Native that retained many web-like UI patterns: browser-style back buttons, web-style dropdown selects, non-native scrolling behavior, text inputs without iOS keyboard accessories, and hamburger menu instead of tab bar navigation.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.2 - Design - Minimum Functionality: Your app's user interface does not provide an experience that is consistent with the quality and design expectations of the App Store. The app appears to use web-based UI components that do not conform to iOS Human Interface Guidelines. Please review the iOS Human Interface Guidelines and ensure your app provides a native-quality experience.
stories.fix: Replaced web-style components with native-looking equivalents: used bottom tab navigation instead of hamburger menu, native-style action sheets instead of web dropdowns, proper iOS navigation bar with back chevron, native scrolling with rubber-banding, and iOS-style form inputs with proper keyboard handling.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app is a duplicate of another app and does not provide a unique experience.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Submitted an app that was a fork of the open-source RxMarbles app with the same binary, same functionality, and only cosmetic changes (icon color). The app was submitted from a different developer account than the original.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.3 - Design - Spam: Your app duplicates the content and functionality of another app already on the App Store (RxMarbles). Submitting multiple similar apps or copycat versions of popular apps is considered spam. Please ensure your app provides a unique, innovative experience.
stories.fix: This rejection is not easily fixable since the app was fundamentally a duplicate. The developer would need to create a genuinely unique app with different functionality and value proposition. Simply changing the skin or branding of an existing app is insufficient.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app impersonates or copies another developer's app or service.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: After OpenAI announced Sora (AI video generation), dozens of copycat apps appeared on the App Store with names like 'Sora 2 AI Video', 'Sora Video Generator Pro', and similar variations. These apps used the Sora name and branding to mislead users, often charging subscriptions for unrelated or non-functional AI services.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.3 - Design - Spam: Your app appears to impersonate or misleadingly suggest an affiliation with another developer's product (Sora/OpenAI). Apps that copy the name, branding, or concept of another product to mislead users are not permitted on the App Store.
stories.fix: These apps were removed from the App Store. Apple conducted a mass removal of Sora copycat apps. Developers of legitimate AI video tools need to use original branding that does not suggest affiliation with OpenAI or Sora.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app's UI elements are inconsistent with iOS design patterns and appear to follow Android design conventions.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Ported an Android app to iOS but kept Android-style Material Design UI elements: floating action buttons (FAB), Android-style bottom sheets, Material Design text fields with floating labels, three-dot overflow menus, and Android-style toggle switches.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.0 - Design: Your app's user interface does not follow iOS design conventions. Several UI elements appear to be designed for another platform. Please review the iOS Human Interface Guidelines and update your app's interface to provide an experience consistent with the iOS platform.
stories.fix: Replaced Android-style UI elements with iOS equivalents: FAB became a navigation bar '+' button, Material bottom sheets became iOS sheet presentations, floating label text fields became standard iOS text fields, three-dot menus became iOS ellipsis menus or swipe actions, and toggle switches were replaced with UISwitch.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app uses third-party social login but does not offer Sign in with Apple as an option.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Implemented Google Sign-In and Facebook Login as authentication options but did not include Sign in with Apple. Since June 2020, apps that offer third-party social login must also offer Sign in with Apple as an equivalent option.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.8 - Design - Sign in with Apple: Your app uses third-party login services (Google, Facebook) but does not offer Sign in with Apple. Apps that use a third-party or social login service to set up or authenticate the user's primary account must also offer Sign in with Apple as an equivalent option.
stories.fix: Added Sign in with Apple as a login option alongside Google and Facebook. Implemented the AuthenticationServices framework with ASAuthorizationAppleIDProvider. Ensured the Sign in with Apple button is displayed with equal prominence to other login options.
behavioralSignals: missing Sign in with Apple button

stories.rejectionReason: Your Sign in with Apple button does not follow Apple's Human Interface Guidelines for button styling.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Implemented Sign in with Apple but used a custom-styled button that didn't match Apple's required design specifications. The button was too small, used a custom font, had rounded corners that didn't match the spec, and was placed below other login options in a smaller size.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.8 - Design - Sign in with Apple: Your Sign in with Apple button does not conform to the required design specifications. The button must use Apple's provided styles (ASAuthorizationAppleIDButton), be at least the same size as other login buttons, and follow the Human Interface Guidelines for Sign in with Apple button design.
stories.fix: Replaced the custom button with Apple's native ASAuthorizationAppleIDButton, which automatically handles correct styling, sizing, and localization. Ensured the button is the same size or larger than other login buttons and is positioned with equal prominence on the login screen.
behavioralSignals: Apple login less prominent than others

stories.rejectionReason: Your app uses Apple's copyrighted imagery without authorization.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Used a screenshot of the iOS home screen (SpringBoard) as a background image in the app's onboarding tutorial. The screenshot included Apple's copyrighted wallpaper, app icons, and the dock design.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.5.3 - Design - Apple Trademarks: Your app uses Apple's copyrighted material (iOS home screen screenshot including SpringBoard interface and Apple app icons). You may not use Apple-owned images, icons, or screenshots of Apple software in your app without explicit permission.
stories.fix: Replaced the iOS home screen screenshot with a custom-designed illustration that conveys the same tutorial concept without using Apple's copyrighted imagery. Used generic device mockups from Apple's official marketing resources (which are permitted for certain uses) or created original artwork.
behavioralSignals: iOS home screen screenshot in app

stories.rejectionReason: Your app provides functionality that is too similar to built-in iOS apps without providing additional unique value.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Created a simple calculator app and a flashlight app that replicated the exact functionality of iOS built-in apps without any additional features, customization options, or unique value proposition.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.2 - Design - Minimum Functionality: Your app replicates the functionality of a built-in iOS app (Calculator/Flashlight) without providing additional unique value. Simple utility apps that duplicate built-in capabilities are not appropriate for the App Store unless they offer significant additional functionality.
stories.fix: For the calculator: added scientific calculator mode, unit conversion, calculation history, custom themes, and a widget. For the flashlight: added SOS mode, color filters, strobe patterns, screen color options, and an ambient light meter. The apps now offer meaningful functionality beyond the built-in equivalents.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app does not provide a unique or innovative experience and lacks sufficient functionality.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Submitted a very simple app with a single screen that performed one basic function (e.g., a tip calculator with just a percentage slider and total display) without any additional features, customization, or polish.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.2 - Design - Minimum Functionality: Your app does not include sufficient content or functionality to provide a compelling App Store experience. We encourage you to review your app concept and add more features and content to provide value to users.
stories.fix: Expanded the app with multiple features: bill splitting, custom tip presets, receipt scanning, expense history, group dining calculations, Apple Watch companion, and widgets. The app evolved from a single-function utility to a comprehensive dining expense tool.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app's interactive elements are too small for comfortable touch interaction.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Designed an app with very small buttons (less than 44x44 points), tiny text (below 11pt), and densely packed interactive elements that were difficult to tap accurately on iPhone screens.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.0 - Design: Your app includes interactive elements that are too small for reliable touch interaction. Per Human Interface Guidelines, tappable elements should have a minimum target size of 44x44 points. Several buttons and links in your app are significantly below this minimum.
stories.fix: Increased all tappable elements to at least 44x44 points. Increased body text to at least 13pt and added Dynamic Type support. Added proper spacing between interactive elements. Tested on the smallest supported iPhone screen size to ensure all elements are comfortably tappable.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app's launch screen displays content in a different language than the app's primary localization.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Created a Japanese-language app but the LaunchScreen.storyboard contained English text ('Loading...', company name in English). The launch screen language didn't match the app's primary language, creating an inconsistent first impression.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.0 - Design: Your app's launch screen contains text in English, but the app's primary language is Japanese. The launch screen should be consistent with the app's primary language and localization.
stories.fix: Localized the LaunchScreen.storyboard to display Japanese text. Best practice: use a minimal launch screen with just the app logo/icon without text to avoid localization issues entirely, matching Apple's own app launch screens.

stories.rejectionReason: Your macOS app does not properly handle window management. Closing all windows provides no way to create a new window.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Built a macOS Catalyst or native macOS app that, when the user closed all windows, had no File > New Window menu item and no dock icon click handler to reopen the main window. The app was running but had no visible UI and no way to get back to it.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.0 - Design: Your macOS app does not properly handle window management. After closing the app's window, there is no menu option to reopen or create a new window. Users expect to be able to click the dock icon or use the File menu to access the app again.
stories.fix: Implemented applicationShouldHandleReopen(_:hasVisibleWindows:) delegate method to show the main window when the dock icon is clicked. Added File > New Window menu item. Ensured the app activates and shows the main window when launched via Spotlight or dock.

stories.rejectionReason: Your app's interface has significant quality issues including spelling errors, grammar mistakes, and unpolished UI elements.
stories.whatDeveloperDid: Submitted an app with multiple spelling errors in button labels and navigation titles, grammatically incorrect alert messages, inconsistent font sizes, misaligned UI elements, and truncated text that made the app feel unfinished and unprofessional.
stories.whatAppleSaid: Guideline 4.0 - Design: Your app's user interface has quality issues that affect the user experience. We found multiple spelling errors ('Settigns', 'Purchse'), grammatically incorrect messages, truncated labels, and misaligned elements. Please polish your app's interface before resubmitting.
stories.fix: Conducted a thorough UI review: fixed all spelling and grammar errors, ensured consistent typography, fixed all layout and alignment issues, tested on all screen sizes to prevent truncation, and had a native speaker review all user-facing text.

stories.guidelineName: Data Use and Sharing - Required Reason APIs
stories.rejectionReason: Your app does not include the required PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy manifest file.
